title: Sebi proposes easing disclosure norms For FPIs
summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) plans to streamline compliance for foreign portfolio investors in the nation. Current disclosure rules pose operational hurdles that may dissuade investment from abroad. By adjusting regulations to meet global standards, SEBI aims to bolster competitiveness. Furthermore, policies regarding investment size and concentration are identified as obstacles. The goal is to attract increased foreign capital through the relaxation of these stipulations.

title: FPIs may soon get to onboard in 5 days, says Tuhin Kanta Pandey, as Sebi moves to reduce compliance burden
summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India is making strides to enable foreign portfolio investors to onboard in just five days. They aim to release a paper that reevaluates existing compliance measures. New initiatives will streamline processes and lengthen KYC review timelines for qualified FPIs. Additionally, the onboarding procedure for non-resident Indians and foreign nationals has been made easier, boosting international capital flow and boosting opportunities for Indian enterprises.

title: Sebi plans limiting tenures for managing directors of stock exchanges, market infrastructure institutions
summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has introduced new regulations to govern managing directors of market infrastructure institutions. These regulations propose a 12-year cap on tenures aimed at avoiding excessive concentration of power. To ease the transition, current managing directors will have a 15-year adjustment period. SEBI underscores the critical role of board independence for effective governance, intending to boost regulatory efficiency and accountability within these institutions.

title: Capital markets need to drive rural infra, says CEA Anantha Nageswaran
summary: Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran emphasized the need for patient capital to develop rural infrastructure. He highlighted how the current financing trends focus on long-term debt rather than equity funding. Nageswaran also mentioned the necessity of assessing creditworthiness based on cash flows for small manufacturers. He raised concerns about the accessibility of capital markets for entrepreneurs seeking long-term financing.

title: Indian stock market indices detour Asian rout(e) to touch 9-month high
summary: India's stock market outperformed other Asia-Pacific markets on Friday, with strong gains in Nifty and Sensex indices. The Sensex rose by more than 800 points, reaching its highest level in nine months. Investors in Japan and South Korea faced declines, influenced by valuation concerns in AI-linked stocks. Despite this, India attracted over $10 billion in overseas fund flows this month, significantly buoying its equities.
